correctness.rationale: The diagonal least-squares normal equation, conditional Gaussian variance, inverse chi-square moment, spherical cosine-square moment, and pairwise shared-query covariance yield the exact formula for every finite \(n\) and \(q\ge3\). A multivariate CLT for \((g_r h_r,h_r^2-g_r^2)\), LLN and Slutsky give the near-skew product-normal limit; its characteristic function is calculated conditionally. Supplementary extracted verifier runs 2021 checks; they are not substituted for proof. No claim of a theorem for \(q\le2\) or a general growing-dimension limit.

originality.rationale: The rowwise least-squares method and normalized Gaussian diagonal estimator are prior art. Compared full motivating and closest earlier original works by mathematical implication: Gallmeier–Otto provides Frobenius bounds, Amsel et al. individual rowwise bounds, Hallman et al. the marginal normalized-Gaussian Student law under symmetry. None of those statements determines the cross-row covariance A_ij A_ji/q for nonsymmetric matrices, exact symmetric/skew trace variance, or the two-dimensional non-Gaussian near-skew crossover. Six actual published-finding corpus semantic searches identified related but noncovering records; prior own claims on Gaussian sketching and trace recovery do not imply this one. The open 2005 preprint of Bekas et al. was obtained and inspected in the original estimator sections, including Eq. 3; no direct cross-covariance or near-skew limit was found there. Equivalent results from other unindexed sources remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2005 open Bekas–Kokiopoulou–Saad preprint was checked, but a different later journal revision or unindexed diagonal-estimation paper might contain an equivalent cross-row trace risk identity.
The product-normal crossover may be derivable from previously published general results for ratios of Gaussian quadratic statistics not retrieved in the literature searches.

value.rationale: Trace readouts of rowwise Gaussian operator surrogates are a natural derived invariant. Exact signed covariance creates symmetry-dependent \(q^{-1}\) versus \(q^{-2}\) mean-square scaling that cannot be read off from per-row Frobenius risk. The non-Gaussian product-normal limit gives a critical regime for uncertainty calibration if an existing surrogate is reused for trace evaluation; the result does not claim to outperform direct Hutchinson trace estimation.
